record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Is every orderable group H embeddable in an orderable group G so that any G-invariant partial order on H has an extention to a total order on G?

evidence.quote: 3.19. (A.I. Kokorin [46] Problem 19) Is every orderable group H embeddable in an orderable group G so that any G-invariant partial order on H has an extention to a total order on G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $H$ is called orderable if there exists a total order $\le$ on $H$ that is bi-invariant, i.e. $a\le b$ implies $xay\le xby$ for all $x,y,a,b\in H$. If $H$ is a subgroup of a group $G$, a partial order $\preceq$ on $H$ is called $G$-invariant if it is preserved under conjugation by every element of $G$, i.e. $a\preceq b$ implies $gag^{-1}\preceq gbg^{-1}$ for all $g\in G$ and all $a,b\in H$ (and $\preceq$ is also bi-invariant under multiplication within $H$).

Question: Is it true that every orderable group $H$ can be embedded into some orderable group $G$ with the following property: every $G$-invariant partial order on $H$ extends to a bi-invariant total order on $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in compilations of unsolved problems on ordered and orderable groups (originally posed as Kokorin's Problem 19) and is still listed as open. Web searches and standard references on orderable groups (Clay–Rolfsen, Deroin, etc.) do not indicate a known resolution.
